title: The Advantage Is What You Do With AI

seo.description: Discover how Wharton's MBA develops leaders who combine AI fluency with rigorous business judgment, research, and practice.

sections.eyebrow: THE WHARTON MBA · AI AND LEADERSHIP
sections.heading: The Advantage Is What You Do With AI.
sections.text: AI is changing the work. Wharton prepares you to rethink how work gets done, build what comes next, and lead with judgment.

sections.eyebrow: THE CASE FOR A WHARTON MBA
sections.heading: Access to AI is universal. The ability to lead with it is not.
sections.quote: AI can give you an answer. The real question is whether you know what to ask, how to challenge the result, and what to do next. At Wharton, we develop the business judgment to turn powerful tools into better decisions—and the leadership to take responsibility for them.
sections.role: Vice Dean of the MBA Program
sections.approvalNote: Draft quote — pending Michael Roberts’ approval

sections.heading: The future needs more than AI proficiency.
sections.text: Michael Roberts, Vice Dean of the MBA Program, makes the case for an education that develops builders, critical thinkers, and leaders. A new page-exclusive film is planned; this production slot is deliberately not the same edit used in the admissions email series.

sections.heading: The skills that separate good answers from consequential decisions.

items.title: Think beyond the output
items.description: Interrogate assumptions, evaluate evidence, and determine what an AI-generated answer gets right and what it misses.

items.title: Build solutions
items.description: Combine technical fluency with business expertise to create useful new tools, capabilities, and ways of working.

items.title: Own the decision
items.description: Communicate the reasoning, earn alignment, and take responsibility for the results when the stakes are real.

sections.heading: Rigor is how your advantage gets built.
sections.text: Wharton is not designed around finding the quickest answer. Faculty push students to defend reasoning, test assumptions, debate trade-offs, and communicate decisions. Through demanding analysis, practical problem-solving, and teamwork, students develop judgment that remains valuable even as the tools evolve.

sections.heading: Research. Industry. Classroom. Repeat.
sections.text: Wharton faculty do not operate in separate worlds as researchers, teachers, and practitioners. They bring questions from industry into research, test insights with executives, and carry new discoveries into the classroom. Students challenge those ideas, generating new questions for the next cycle.

stages.label: Research
stages.description: Discover what AI makes possible and where its limits matter.

stages.label: Practice
stages.description: Work directly with organizations and executives confronting change.

stages.label: Classroom
stages.description: Turn emerging insight into rigorous, applied learning.

sections.eyebrow: SCALE WITH THE INSTINCT TO MOVE
sections.heading: A large institution. An entrepreneurial mindset.
sections.text: Wharton's scale connects MBA students to faculty expertise across disciplines and alumni across industries. Its agility brings emerging technologies into students' hands while they still matter. As the frontier changes, the learning experience can change with it.

sections.eyebrow: THE PROOF IS IN THE EXPERIENCE
sections.heading: AI isn't a distant subject. It's part of the MBA experience.

items.title: Tools for doing the work
items.description: MBA students are introduced to AI during Pre-Term, with school-supported access to ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, and Claude Code. Faculty expectations for responsible classroom use still apply.

items.title: Faculty-led AI workshops
items.description: Michael Roberts joined Ethan Mollick, Kartik Hosanagar, and Daniel Rock in practical workshops designed to share how faculty use AI in professional and personal work.

items.title: A dedicated AI MBA major
items.description: The Artificial Intelligence for Business major connects technical understanding with the economic, strategic, ethical, and organizational questions that shape business decisions.

sections.heading: From learning AI to building something new.
sections.text: In Wharton's Generative AI Studio, Hetvee Marviya, WG'27, is developing an AI-powered platform that transforms current events into personalized comic strips for children. The Studio emphasizes prototyping, feedback, and iteration: students create, test, and improve rather than simply study what's possible. A new student-film interview can bring this section to life in a future production round.

sections.heading: An education that keeps opening doors.
sections.text: Erika Lawrence, WG'23, describes how the Wharton MBA expanded her career ambitions and connected her to a global community. This published alumni video provides the graduate's perspective on long-term value, complementing Roberts' argument for the degree.

sections.heading: The value isn't measured only at graduation.
sections.text: An MBA is an investment in what you can contribute over the course of a career: the problems you're equipped to solve, the people you're prepared to lead, and the community you can continue to learn from. Those are advantages designed to compound.
